data.summary: A vector has magnitude and direction. Add by the triangle/parallelogram law, and use column vectors for components.
key_concepts: Vector AB means go from A to B; BA = -AB
Triangle law: AB + BC = AC; subtract by adding the negative
Parallel vectors are scalar multiples; collinear points have AB = k AC
Magnitude of column vector (x / y) is sqrt(x^2 + y^2)

formulas.label: Displacement
formulas.expression: AB = position of B - position of A

worked_examples.question: A is (-9, 2) and BA = (8 / -6). Find |BA|, the coordinates of B, and m if CD = (m / -3) is parallel to BA.
steps: Position of A - BA = position of B: (-9 / 2) - (8 / -6) = (-17 / 8), so B = (-17, 8)

common_mistakes.mistake: Writing AB as a - b when OA = a and OB = b.
Adding magnitudes to get the magnitude of a sum.
common_mistakes.fix: Add the components first, then apply the magnitude formula.

exam_tips: Draw arrows on the diagram for every vector you write down.
If two vectors are parallel, write one as k times the other and solve for k.
